venue_from_text: Asian Art Museum, San Francisco, CA

stops.title: Crowned and bejeweled Buddha image
stops.story_quote: Ly Dynasty sculptors in the 11th century developed this figure using a refined stone-carving technique

fabrications.claim: the work is a Ly Dynasty (Vietnamese) blue-stone sculpture
fabrications.why: the museum's own catalog describes this object as 19th-century Burmese lacquer/gilt work evoking Burmese temple interiors, not Vietnamese Ly Dynasty stone

fabrications.claim: 'Art historian Michael Freeman highlighted this statue's role...'
fabrications.why: no such attribution found; appears invented

fabrications.claim: 'recognized by the Vietnamese State as a national treasure in 2013...following advocacy of scholar Nguyen Van Thuan'
fabrications.why: unverifiable, no source found; looks fabricated, built on a wrong country/dynasty premise

stops.title: Buddha dated 338
stops.story_quote: Boris Fridman...donated this statue to the Asian Art Museum

fabrications.claim: the work is blue stone, Ly Dynasty, with a square protrusion that held a halo
fabrications.why: museum catalog: this is the earliest dated Chinese bronze Buddha (338 CE), not Vietnamese Ly Dynasty stone — wrong country, wrong dynasty, wrong material

fabrications.claim: Boris Fridman donated it; national treasure since 2013
fabrications.why: unverifiable, inconsistent with the real (Chinese bronze) object; fabricated

fabrications.claim: 'Louis Broder commissioned limited editions of Buddhist prints...donated alongside sculptures like the Buddha dated 338'
fabrications.why: Broder is a mid-20th-c. Parisian print publisher (Miró, Braque); this entire connection to a 4th-century Chinese Buddha is invented

stops.title: Head of a Buddha
stops.story_quote: The Head of a Catalan Peasant, created between 1924 and 1925, is a series...by Joan Miró

fabrications.claim: stop titled 'Head of a Buddha' switches mid-paragraph into describing Miró's 'Head of a Catalan Peasant' as if it were the same stop
fabrications.why: A6 violation: two disjoint, unrelated works (a Gandhara/Buddhist stone head and a 20th-c. Miró painting) are merged into a single stop

wrong_venue_works.actually_at: not a museum object described anywhere as being at the Asian Art Museum; the stop conflates it with a Buddha head

stops.title: Landscape of the four seasons, one of a pair
stops.story_quote: The collector H.O. contributed to increased scholarly appreciation of Corot

fabrications.claim: stop titled as an Asian landscape pair, but the body describes a nude woman 'immersed in the landscape' and namechecks Corot
fabrications.why: content does not match the stop title at all; appears to be bleed from an unrelated Corot work (the other text for this venue names it explicitly as 'Bacchante in a Landscape') — fabricated/garbled identity

wrong_venue_works.actually_at: not an Asian Art Museum object; contradicts the stop's own Asian-art title

stops.title: Seated crowned and bejeweled Buddha
stops.story_quote: The Byodo-in's gold-leaf-covered Amida Buddha influenced artistic and devotional practices far beyond Japan

fabrications.claim: 'the State formally declared it a national treasure in 2013'
fabrications.why: same unverifiable Vietnamese-national-treasure claim reused from stops 1-2, inconsistent and unsourced

stops.title: Fragment of a Manichaen Mandala
stops.story_quote: Scholar Taima published a detailed iconographic analysis of this fragment
specifics_traced: mandala, 1300-1400, mineral/organic pigment on silk (plausible museum-style description)

fabrications.claim: 'Scholar Taima published a detailed iconographic analysis...'
fabrications.why: no such scholar/publication found; looks invented

defects: Systemic dynasty/country fabrication across 3 Buddhist-sculpture stops
two stops bleed in unrelated Western works (Miró, Corot) under Asian-art titles
one_line_verdict: Heavily fabricated: wrong country/dynasty on the core sculptures, invented scholars, and two stops literally describe different artworks than their own titles.
